questions.text: At its core, how does a large language model generate text?

options.text: It looks the answer up in a database of verified facts.
It searches the internet for existing text and rewrites it.
It predicts the next token one at a time, based on everything that came before it.
It plans the whole response first, then writes it out.

questions.explanation: The lesson describes an LLM as a next-token prediction machine: it builds the response one token at a time and does not plan its answer in advance.

questions.text: Large language models process whole words in the same way a human reader does.
questions.explanation: LLMs work with tokens — chunks that may be whole words, parts of words or single characters — which is why they sometimes miscount the letters in a word.

questions.text: Which statements about how LLMs are trained are accurate?

options.text: Pre-training means reading enormous amounts of text from the internet, books, articles and code repositories.
Fine-tuning and alignment use human feedback to make the model helpful, safe and better at following instructions.
Training a large model can cost tens of millions of dollars and take months on specialised hardware.
After training, the model keeps a copy of every source document so it can quote them exactly.

questions.explanation: Training happens in two phases — pre-training on vast text, then fine-tuning with human feedback — and it is resource-intensive; but the result is a pattern machine, not a stored library of its sources.

questions.text: What is the "context window" of a language model?

options.text: The area of the screen where the chat is displayed.
The information the model holds during a conversation — its working memory.
The time limit before a conversation expires.
The list of websites the model is allowed to visit.

questions.explanation: Context works like a working memory for the conversation. It is large but not unlimited, so in very long conversations the earliest parts start to drop out and the model appears to forget them.
